clue.text: It goes off when it's on if one's in when you're out

definitions.text: It goes off when it's on if one's in when you're out

parts.words: It goes off when it's on if one's in when you're out
parts.note: a riddle about a security device: when it is set and an intruder gets into the house while the owner is away, it sounds

explanation.surface: A riddling string of little words about something going off, being on, and people being in and out.
explanation.walkthrough: Each small word shifts sense: 'goes off' is sounds, 'on' is switched on, 'one's in' is an intruder inside, 'you're out' is you being away from home.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes a household security device that rings when a burglar enters while it is switched on.

clue.text: Still at the crease, not getting bowled, not taken in

indicators.note: not getting says the bowled letter is left out

parts.note: in cricket a batsman still in at the end is not out, or unbeaten
B is the cricket scoring abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: a batsman surviving at the crease, never bowled out, never caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not taken in' sounds like more cricket but means not eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Food left on the plate is uneaten: it has not been consumed or swallowed.

clue.text: £1000 people put on a new driver in big race

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds
a nation is a people
L is the learner plate shown by a new driver in Britain

explanation.surface: A punter puts a thousand pounds on a novice jockey in a major race.
explanation.walkthrough: The GRAND NATIONAL is Britain's most famous steeplechase horse race, run at Aintree.
explanation.definitionFit: This steeplechase is one of the biggest events in the British horse racing calendar.

clue.text: Without limits, impeded current measure

indicators.note: without limits says the impeded word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: impeded means hampered

explanation.surface: Someone held back on all sides is cut off at the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit of electric current in the SI system is named after Ampère.

clue.text: New notice at canal indicating expanse of water

indicators.note: new says the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh sign by a canal pointing to a large body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean between the Americas and Europe and Africa is a vast stretch of sea.

clue.text: A person from Musselburgh racecourse

parts.note: Musselburgh is a town near Edinburgh, so its people are Scots

explanation.surface: A local from Musselburgh racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Musselburgh has a racecourse itself, which pulls the eye; ASCOT is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is the Berkshire course famous for Royal Ascot week.

clue.text: Messed-up fellow guided to follow leader of group

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: leader of means take the first letter of the group word

parts.note: guided means led

explanation.surface: A confused man is guided along behind the head of the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' just places LED after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangled means badly damaged or garbled, so messed up.

clue.text: Athlete's fitness, perhaps, for mile

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mile; that the letters also run unbroken across these two words is a coincidence of the charade

explanation.surface: An athlete's condition for running a mile.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner in good form is in peak condition; 'perhaps' marks fitness as one sense among several.

clue.text: Piano involved in old time music theatre

indicators.note: involved in says the piano letter is wrapped up inside the following pieces

parts.note: an era is a period of time
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A piano being part of an old-time music hall show.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is staged musical drama, the kind of work a theatre presents with singers and orchestra.

clue.text: Nut circling lake with one waterfowl

indicators.note: circling says the nut goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a pecan is a kind of nut
L is the map abbreviation for lake
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A nut ringed by a lake along with a single bird, a little nature scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelican is a large water bird with a pouched bill, so it is an example of waterfowl.

clue.text: Bullfighter wild about cheers provided by men

indicators.note: about says the word for wild goes around the next piece

parts.note: wild can mean mad, furious
ta is a British informal way to say thanks, like cheers
OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers, men as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: A bullfighter getting wildly excited at the cheers his men give him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' looks like an anagram signal, but it is a synonym, MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the principal performer in a bullfight, the one who makes the kill.

clue.text: Note a story left incomplete, regarding a birth

indicators.note: left incomplete means the story word loses its final letter

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Someone jots down a story but leaves it unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal is the adjective for things relating to being born, as in a natal day.

clue.text: Crazy fellows chatter endlessly

parts.note: fellows are men

indicators.note: endlessly means the chatter word loses its last letter

parts.note: to chatter is to talk

explanation.surface: A complaint that some blokes never stop gabbing, which is driving someone mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental is a colloquial word for mad or unhinged.

clue.text: Girl stifling expression of annoyance over accidents

indicators.note: stifling says the girl word smothers the next piece inside it

parts.note: miss is a word for a girl

indicators.note: over in a down clue says the annoyance word is turned upside down

parts.note: pah is an exclamation of irritation

explanation.surface: A girl swallowing her irritation after mishaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Mishaps and accidents are both unlucky incidents.

clue.text: Clear sign of leg injury I had

parts.note: walking with a limp shows the leg is hurt
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A clear indication of the leg injury someone suffered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear sign' reads as one phrase, but 'Clear' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid describes water or prose that is transparent and easily seen through.

clue.text: Junior soldier to talk boastfully, having captured four

indicators.note: having captured says the talk word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: to prate is to talk foolishly or boastfully at length
IV is the Roman numeral four

explanation.surface: A low-ranking soldier bragging after taking four prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest rank in the British army is the ordinary rank-and-file soldier.

clue.text: Son has the best yell

parts.note: the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop

explanation.surface: A boy has the loudest shout of all.
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is a loud piercing cry, much like a yell.

clue.text: Oriental food keeps us hiccupping to some extent

explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, an example of food from the East.

clue.text: Number of sins still to be overcome by Saint

parts.note: even can mean still, as in even more

explanation.surface: Sins a saint has yet to conquer.

explanation.definitionFit: Christian tradition counts seven deadly sins, so seven is their number.

clue.text: Conservative doing badly and finishing

parts.note: a side doing badly is losing

explanation.surface: A political report: the Tory candidate is faring poorly and finishing the race.
explanation.definitionFit: Closing means bringing to an end, as in the closing stages of a contest.

clue.text: Crowd runs from site of fire

indicators.note: from says the runs letter is taken away from the fire word

parts.note: a grate holds a coal fire in a fireplace
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

clue.text: A volume in Charleston, say, generates payment for author

parts.note: the Charleston is a 1920s dance, so an example of a dance

clue.text: Precise description of repealed legislation

parts.note: ex means former, no longer in force
an act is a piece of legislation

explanation.surface: An accurate account of a law that has been struck off.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact and precise are synonyms meaning accurate in every detail.

clue.text: Intent on not marrying

definitions.meaning: intent means resolutely focused on one goal
minded to stay unmarried, so set on remaining a bachelor or spinster

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: minded to stay single.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: determinedly focused on a purpose, and literally of a mind to remain unwed.
